questions.question: When driving a bobtail tractor, what should you know?

options.text: Bobtails cannot drive as fast as tractors with trailers.
Bobtails are harder to stop than tractors with trailers.
Bobtails are illegal in most states.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bobtails are harder to stop than tractors with trailers.
questions.explanation: A bobtail is a tractor without a trailer attached. Bobtails take longer to stop than tractors pulling a loaded trailer.

questions.question: How do you test the trailer service brakes?

options.text: Move forward slowly and use the brake pedal.
Move backward slowly and use the hand control.
Move backward slowly and use the brake pedal.
Move forward slowly and use the hand control.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward slowly and use the hand control.
questions.explanation: To test the trailer service brakes, first check that the air pressure is normal and release the parking brake. Then move forward slowly and use the hand control. If the brakes work properly, you will feel them activate.

questions.question: Starting in what year were new trailers required to have ABS?
questions.explanation: All trailers made on or after March 1, 1998 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).

questions.question: How do you check that air reaches all trailers before driving?

options.text: Open the rear shut-off valves and listen for air escaping.
Close the rear shut-off valves and listen for air escaping.
Disconnect air supply lines and listen for air escaping.
Roll each trailer down a hill and test the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open the rear shut-off valves and listen for air escaping.
questions.explanation: Before a trip, check that air reaches all trailers. Wait for air pressure to build, then send air to both the emergency and service lines. Open the shut-off valves on the rear of the last trailer. If air escapes from these valves, air is being supplied to the entire vehicle.

questions.question: What happens if you use the trailer hand valve while driving?

options.text: It will help you turn safely.
It will stop your trailer safely.

questions.explanation: Never use the trailer hand valve while driving. Using it while the vehicle is moving can cause your trailer to skid.

questions.question: When should you use the trailer hand valve for parking?

options.text: Only when parking on a hill.

questions.explanation: Never use the trailer hand valve for parking. It can cause all air to leak out of the braking system, which will release the brakes. Use the parking brake instead.

questions.question: What does the trailer air supply control look like?
questions.explanation: On newer vehicles, the trailer air supply control is an eight-sided red knob. It controls the tractor protection valve.

questions.question: In a sudden turn, which trailer is most likely to turn over?
questions.explanation: When turning, steer gently and smoothly. A quick turn while pulling trailers is dangerous and increases the risk that the last trailer will roll over.

questions.question: If you cannot back your trailer in a straight line, which way should you back?
questions.explanation: If you need to back on a curve, back toward the driver's side. This gives you the best visibility while backing.

questions.question: What do you test by putting the trailer air supply control in the "emergency" position?
questions.explanation: Test the trailer emergency brakes before your trip. After checking that the trailer rolls freely, pull out the trailer air supply control or put it in the "emergency" position. Pull forward slightly and make sure the trailer does not move.

questions.question: When pulling a trailer, the air supply control lever should be in what position?
questions.explanation: Some older vehicles have levers instead of knobs for tractor protection controls. The air supply control should be in the "normal" position when you pull a trailer.

questions.question: When driving slower than 40 mph, how much following distance should you keep for every 10 feet of your vehicle?
questions.explanation: Below 40 mph, leave one second of space for every 10 feet of your vehicle. At faster speeds, use the same formula and add one more second. Larger vehicles need more space to stop.

questions.question: Rollovers happen when drivers:
questions.explanation: A rollover happens when a driver takes a turn at too high a speed. Take all turns and curves slowly and carefully.

questions.question: When coupling glad hands, at what angle should the seals be pressed together?
questions.explanation: When connecting glad hands, press the seals together at a 90-degree angle.

questions.question: To reduce rollover risk, you should:

options.text: Load cargo as far forward as possible
Load cargo as far back as possible
Load cargo as low as possible
Stack cargo as high as possible

questions.correctAnswerText: Load cargo as low as possible
questions.explanation: Load your cargo as close to the ground as possible to reduce rollover risk. Also take curves and corners slowly.

questions.question: Why does a lightly-loaded combination vehicle stop more slowly than a fully-loaded vehicle?

options.text: Stiff suspension springs and strong brakes create high traction
Stiff suspension springs and strong brakes create low traction
Brakes only work when a trailer reaches minimum weight
Suspension springs only work when a trailer reaches minimum weight

questions.correctAnswerText: Stiff suspension springs and strong brakes create low traction
questions.explanation: An empty combination vehicle takes longer to stop than a fully-loaded one. Stiff suspension springs and strong brakes have less traction with a light load.

questions.question: What happens when the air supply control is in the "emergency" position?

options.text: The trailer emergency brakes will be applied
The air supply to the trailer will increase

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer emergency brakes will be applied
questions.explanation: Some older vehicles have levers instead of knobs for tractor protection controls. In the "emergency" position, air supply stops and the trailer emergency brakes activate.

questions.question: Trailers made after what year must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS)?
questions.explanation: All trailers and converter dollies made on or after March 1, 1998 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).

questions.question: What is a bobtail tractor?

options.text: A tractor that travels faster than the speed limit

questions.explanation: A bobtail tractor is a tractor without a semi-trailer attached. These vehicles are difficult to operate and require careful handling.

questions.question: What happens if the emergency air line loses pressure?

options.text: The Anti-Lock Braking System will activate
The service air line will activate

questions.explanation: The emergency air line controls the emergency brakes. If pressure is lost in this line, the trailer emergency brakes will automatically activate.
